summary: This revision directly responds to all three round-1 weaknesses on a synthetic 'capital city' QA task with known ground-truth ambiguity: it replicates the main lexical-vs-oracle-semantic entropy AUROC comparison across 5 seeds (1.000±0.000 vs 0.987±0.011), adds a targeted class-correlated alias-diversity ablation (3 seeds) that stress-tests the paper's own 'additive offset' explanation for the round-1 null result (semantic AUROC narrows from 0.987 to 0.970 but does not overtake lexical), and quantifies OOD-vs-in-distribution separability with AUROC (semantic entropy 0.888±0.074, unmapped-rate proxy 0.584±0.156). It also candidly revises its own original length-confound claim: multi-seed replication shows the previously-reported near-zero correlation was a single-seed artifact, and the true correlation is noisy (lexical mean r=0.29, std=0.17).
strengths:
- All three round-1 weaknesses are addressed with actual new experiments rather than just discussion text: 5-seed replication of the main AUROC comparison, a genuinely adversarial class-correlated alias ablation designed to break the paper's own proposed mechanism, and quantitative OOD AUROC (0.888±0.074 for semantic entropy vs. 0.584±0.156 for the unmapped-rate proxy) in place of the round-1 qualitative-only OOD claim.
- Every headline number in the text (AUROC 1.000±0.000 / 0.987±0.011 for experiment A, 0.999±0.001 / 0.970±0.017 for experiment B, corr_len_lex 0.29±0.17 / corr_len_sem −0.09±0.21, OOD AUROC 0.888±0.074 / 0.584±0.156) is verified to match results_v2.json exactly, and the reported n_seeds_lex_ge_sem=5/5 and 3/3 are also consistent with the per-seed rows in the JSON.
- Unusually honest self-correction: rather than quietly dropping or reframing the original 'no length confound' claim, the paper explicitly flags it as an artifact of single-seed noise and reports the weaker, corrected finding — a good-faith response to exactly the kind of statistical fragility round-1 raised, and it strengthens rather than undermines the paper's credibility.
weaknesses:
- The class-correlated alias ablation (§4b), the most direct test of the paper's central mechanistic claim, is explicitly acknowledged to be confounded by city overlap between ambiguous and deterministic country answer sets ('some deterministic questions inherit a high-alias-count city'), so the 0.987→0.970 narrowing is only suggestive, not a clean causal test of the offset mechanism — the paper flags this honestly but does not attempt the cleaner class-exclusive variant it identifies as the fix, despite the ~20-40s per-run cost that made 8 total runs feasible for the other revisions.
- The temperature ablation (§4d) remains an unreplicated single-seed result carried over verbatim from v1, so the one ablation round-1 did not specifically flag is now the weakest-evidenced claim in the paper by construction, sitting awkwardly next to the newly variance-aware tables around it.
- The paper still does not implement or compare against a real NLI-based clustering baseline even within the synthetic world (acknowledged explicitly as scope-narrowing in Discussion), so despite the added rigor, the central comparison remains 'lexical entropy vs. an oracle upper bound on semantic clustering,' not vs. any actual semantic-entropy implementation — this was flagged in round 1 as narrowing ecological validity and is unchanged in this revision, just more explicitly caveated.
questions:
1. Given that the class-correlated alias ablation's city-overlap confound is identified but not fixed, how large is the affected subset (how many of the 25 deterministic countries inherit a city also used by an ambiguous country), and would results change materially if those were excluded from the AUROC computation?
2. Was there a specific reason the temperature ablation was not re-run across even 2-3 seeds given that each full run only takes 20-45 seconds and 8 total runs were already budgeted for the other revisions — was this a late-stage time constraint rather than a validity judgment?
3. Does the revised, noisier length-confound finding (lexical mean r=0.29, std=0.17) change your view on whether a real length-entropy confound could exist in this synthetic design after all, given that some individual seeds show r as high as ~0.60 per the paper's own text?
